claim: The retained Erdős 180 statement asks the unrestricted finite-family compactness question, while CompactnessConjecture.CompactnessConjectureStatement formalizes the manuscript's corrected nonempty cyclic-family restriction. The predicates are not identical. However, quantitativeCompactnessCounterexample constructs a nonempty family of connected bipartite cyclic graphs that violates compactness, so the formal result supplies a counterexample to both the corrected conjecture and the broader retained question.

retained_problem_statement.statement: For every finite family F of finite graphs, does some G in F satisfy ex(n;G) = O_F(ex(n;F))?

manuscript.reference: Chapter 10, Section 1.1 and Theorem 1.1, printed page 235; PDF page 237

reproduction_evidence.observed: The exact profile passed Comparator, Nanoda, and Lean's default kernel in the retained hardened network-disabled Linux replay; all three declarations depend exactly on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.

evidence: FiniteGraph packages a finite labeled simple graph, and a Finset FiniteGraph represents a finite graph family.
FamilyFree requires a host to contain no member as a subgraph; familyExtremal takes the maximum edge count over family-free graphs on Fin n.

IsCompactFamily asks for one member and a positive constant whose single-graph extremal number is eventually at most that constant times the family extremal number, matching the retained constant-factor relation for a fixed family.
IsCyclicFamily requires every member to contain a cycle; this definition is internally faithful to the manuscript's corrected formulation but is absent from the retained statement.
The retained wording quantifies over every finite family and does not state the manuscript's cyclic-family restriction.
CompactnessConjectureStatement quantifies only over nonempty finite families whose every member contains a cycle.
Explicit nonemptiness resolves the otherwise impossible empty-family existential and matches the manuscript's corrected question.
The missing cyclic-family condition is substantive, not cosmetic: the manuscript says the unrestricted original has simple counterexamples before introducing the corrected conjecture.
The Lean conjecture adds the manuscript's requirement that every forbidden graph contain a cycle.
The quantitative witness is stronger still: every family member is connected and bipartite as well as cyclic.
Those stronger witness properties do not repair literal predicate identity, but they ensure the constructed family is also a valid family for the unrestricted retained question.
The manuscript and Lean prove a family-level upper bound O(n^(4/3-1/48)) and an Omega(n^(4/3)) lower bound for every individual member.
The exponent gap implies that no member has extremal number within a constant factor of the family extremal number.
not_erdos_180 negates the corrected cyclic-family predicate.

Because the same explicit family is finite and violates compactness, quantitativeCompactnessCounterexample also provides a counterexample to the broader retained question even though no separate unrestricted predicate is declared.
The teorth/erdosproblems observation was last updated on 2025-08-31 and records problem 180 as open and unformalized.
The pinned OpenAI release is dated 2026-08-01 and explicitly distinguishes the easy counterexamples to the original formulation from its counterexample to the corrected cyclic-family conjecture.
The retained source statement preserves the unrestricted wording and therefore does not yet expose the corrected hypothesis boundary.

A source-owning correction should decide whether Erdős 180's retained statement is meant to record the original unrestricted question, the corrected nonempty cyclic-family conjecture, or both as separately timed formulations.

Until that correction is explicit, the formal result should be described as refuting the corrected cyclic-family conjecture and, by its stronger witness, also answering the unrestricted question negatively.
